land.text: Bytom, partitioned from the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz in c. 1281; Casimir's formal division with his brother Bolko I of Opole came in 1284

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Duchy of Opole row (1177-1304) is the undivided Opole-Racibórz duchy and Bolko I's Opole after 1284.

land.text: the whole duchy, merged with Opole under Jan II the Good in 1498

successors.note: Infobox 'Merged with Opole: 1498'. From 1472 Matthias Corvinus held Bytom (annexed, pledged to Jan of Zierotin); the page does not say how it came back to Jan II.

capitals.name: Bytom
capitals.note: The page names Bytom as the capital. Coordinates are those of the gazetteer's Bytom; the page gives none.

correction.text: Bytom, the capital, in the partition of the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz 'about 1281'; the formal division with Bolko I that gave Casimir Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice and Siewierz came only in 1284

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Bytom shape starts in 1285 but the Duchy of Bytom page dates the partition to about 1281 (infobox 'Partitioned from Opole and Racibórz: 1281'). Casimir of Bytom says he ruled jointly with Bolko I from 1282 to 1284, so the 1281-1283 extent is only the core. Neither page gives an area.

correction.text: Casimir received Bytom with Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice and Siewierz at the 1284 division: the Cliopatria shape plus Toszek and Siewierz

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 2,085 km2 shape holds Bytom, Gliwice and the Koźle area (a gazetteer test with a 15 km disc at Koźle gives one cell) but not Toszek or Siewierz, which the Casimir page names. Neither page gives an infobox area, so the size check is not possible.

correction.text: the same shape as 1285-1293 plus Toszek and Siewierz

keyframe_review.note: Same correction as the 1285 shape; the shape is unchanged from 1293. On 1303 the Casimir page says 'Casimir decided to give his sons separate districts' (Bolesław Toszek, Władysław Koźle) and the Duchy page's infobox says 'Split off Koźle and Toszek: 1303'; the later 1355 sentence still counts Koźle as Bytom's north, so the districts are read as family appanages and the shape is not cut.

correction.text: carried forward from the corrected 1294 shape; the Duchy of Bytom page gives no boundary for these years

keyframe_review.note: unverified: page budget. New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Bytom row after 1304 although the duchy lasted to 1498. The page records only rulers and holders: the Bytom Piast line ends in 1355, the north (with Koźle) goes to Konrad I of Oleśnica and the rest to Casimir I of Cieszyn, the duchy is divided between Oleśnica and Cieszyn 1357-1459 and reunited under Oleśnica in 1459. The undivided shape is drawn; the Oleśnica and Cieszyn halves are in the notes.

region.text: Bytom, the capital; the page gives no extent before 1284

ledger.note: c. 1281: the Duchy of Bytom is partitioned from the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz. The page says the duchy was established 'about 1281' when the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz was split among the sons of Władysław Opolski; the Casimir page puts Władysław's death in 1282 and the formal division in 1284.

region.text: Bytom with Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice and Siewierz

ledger.note: 1284: Casimir takes Bytom with Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice and Siewierz (the Casimir page: from 1284 he was Duke of Bytom, which he received with these towns). 'The common rule between them lasted until 1284, when they decided to make a formal division of their domains' (Casimir and his brother Bolko I of Opole); the Duchy page has 'Casimir sole ruler: 1284'.

1355: the Bytom Piast line dies out and the duchy passes to other Piast houses. The page: the Bytom line died out with Bolesław, his widow Margareta of Sternberg ceded the north, including Koźle, to Konrad I of Oleśnica, and the rest went to Casimir I of Cieszyn. Dukes of Cieszyn and Oleśnica then rule Bytom (divided 1357-1459, reunited under Oleśnica 1459). Treated as a dynasty change within the same state; the split of the land is not drawn (see notes).

region.text: the whole duchy, annexed and pledged to Jan of Zierotin

ledger.note: 1472: Matthias Corvinus annexes Bytom. The page: Matthias Corvinus, who had declared himself King of Bohemia, annexed Bytom and pledged it to Jan of Zierotin. The page names him 'Matthias Corvinus of Hungary, then self-declared King of Bohemia', so Hungary is the counterpart; confidence stays 2 because he held Silesia as claimant King of Bohemia. The pledge lasts to the merger with Opole in 1498.

1498: the Duchy of Bytom is merged back into the Duchy of Opole under Jan II the Good (infobox 'Merged with Opole: 1498'). The land had been annexed by Matthias Corvinus and pledged to Jan of Zierotin since 1472 (page), so it passes to Opole from that pledge, not from this duchy's own hands: the dossier that holds the pledged land in 1497 (kingdom-of-hungary, by this dossier's 1472 loss) must carry the 1498 loss to duchy-of-opole.

1498: end of the Duchy of Bytom, merged with Opole. The page's later notes (1526 Louis II enfeoffs George of Brandenburg-Ansbach with Bytom; Habsburg state country; Prussia annexes it in 1742) belong to other states.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on either page; the duchy is a set of named towns (Bytom, Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice, Siewierz) and the borders are approximate throughout.

sources.title: Duchy of Bytom
sources.note: Identity, c. 1281 partition, capital Bytom, 1289 vassalage, 1303 split, 1355, 1472, 1498 merger. No area and no infobox size.

sources.title: Casimir of Bytom
sources.note: 1282-1284 co-rule, the 1284 division (Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice, Siewierz), the 10 January 1289 homage at Prague, the 1303 districts for his sons, death 10 March 1312.

notes: Duchy of Bytom, eu-15-i, 2 pages (budget 1-2). (1) Start: the Duchy page says about 1281 (infobox 1281); Casimir of Bytom says joint rule 1282-1284 and the formal division in 1284; Cliopatria starts 1285. The dossier starts 1281 with a core keyframe, the 1284 event carries the growth to the Cliopatria shape. (2) Vassalage: on 10 January 1289 at Prague 'Casimir was the first Silesian Duke to pay homage to the Bohemian King Wenceslaus II in Prague' (Casimir page; Duchy page: 'Vassalized by Bohemia: 1289'). This is a vassal_start for counterpart duchy-of-bytom that belongs in the kingdom-of-bohemia ledger (other agent); nothing in the pages opened ends it before 1498, and Bohemia's rights over Bytom after Wenceslaus II are not dated on these pages. (3) 1303: the Duchy page says the duchy 'lost Koźle and Toszek' and the Casimir page that he gave his sons separate districts (Bolesław Toszek, Władysław Koźle); the 1355 sentence still counts Koźle as Bytom's. Read as appanages, not as loss to another state. (4) 1305-1471 is carried forward from the corrected 1294 shape because Cliopatria stops in 1304 and the page gives no boundaries (unverified: page budget); the 1355-1459 division between the Oleśnica and Cieszyn houses (north with Koźle to Oleśnica, the rest to Cieszyn) is not drawn. The eu-15-x additions batch, which owns the Polish duchies of 1304-1370, may refine it. (5) 1472-1497: Matthias Corvinus annexed Bytom and pledged it to Jan of Zierotin; the dossier records a loss to Hungary and no Bytom shape for 1472-1497 (the land is Hungarian in that interval); the Hungary dossier should carry the matching gain. (6) Rulers omitted: the Duchy page's list of rulers is garbled (Konrad VII the White with a 1316 start, Wacław I with 1431/1442-1459, overlapping Władysław 1316-1352 and George 1316-1327). (7) No war: the Battle of Siewierz of 26 February 1289 is only mentioned on the Casimir page as a possible cause and was not opened. (8) Gazetteer names needed: Toszek, Siewierz, Koźle (places; Koźle = Kędzierzyn-Koźle area, c. 18.2 E 50.34 N; Toszek c. 18.6 E 50.45 N; Siewierz c. 19.2 E 50.46 N). (9) No infobox area on any page opened, so the factor-of-two check against Cliopatria's 2,085 km2 could not be made.
